minor.issue: PRE-EXISTING test data leak — manual po_number 'MASCI-9999' was inserted by a prior run and the unique partial-index on po_number now triggers DuplicateKeyError 500 when this test re-runs. Not introduced by iter153B. Mitigation: either teardown should drop po_requests where po_number='MASCI-9999' OR generate a unique manual po_number per run (e.g. f'MASCI-9999-{uuid[:6]}').

action_items: (Minor) In /app/backend/tests/test_iter153_po_requests.py::test_approve_with_manual_po_number_override change the manual override constant from a static 'MASCI-9999' to a per-run unique value (e.g. f'MASCI-9999-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}'), OR add a module teardown that deletes po_requests with po_number startswith 'MASCI-9999'. Issue is a stale-state leak, not a regression from iter153B.

Clarification block is gated to requester || admin — HR (approver) correctly does NOT see the block when reviewing a Clarification Needed PO, which is the intended workflow.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter156 / Phase 2.5 PO Completeness is GREEN. Critical route ordering (export.csv BEFORE /{po_id}) is preserved. The only loose end is a pre-existing data-leak failure in test_iter153_po_requests.py::test_approve_with_manual_po_number_override (uses static po_number 'MASCI-9999' which collides with prior runs via the partial unique index). Suggest making that constant unique per run.
rca of the issue: N/A for iter153B (all green). For the iter153 leak: the test posts {po_number_manual: 'MASCI-9999'} on every run, but the partial unique index on po_requests.po_number (partialFilterExpression: type==string) treats every assigned MASCI-9999 as a uniqueness conflict on re-run. Two reasonable fixes: (a) parameterize the manual override per-run with a uuid suffix, or (b) delete po_requests where po_number starts with 'MASCI-9999' in the module-scope teardown.
